surfaces.part: gabled roof, left and right slopes
wall with roller door and wooden door

answer.evidence: The roof is two sloped planes with shingle rows, rising from a width of 3 at row 6 to the full width of 138 at row 26. The planes end in a light eave edge line, with a dark outline and shadow just below it, which is evidence (c). The roof is about 41 rows tall at the center column and runs to about row 59 at the sides. Below it is a vertical south wall of about 52 rows with a roller door, a wooden door and a vent. The wall is a front face and the roof is a clear top surface, so this is a three-quarter view.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate has 6 visible tones per 16x16 tile against 12 and 10 in the references, and only 23 distinct colours in total against 185 and 66. Its roof is grey with horizontal banding and a ridge highlight, and the walls are corrugated vertical stripes, which gives some texture and no large flat fills (0% near-flat). But each material has only about 3-4 lightness steps, and the roof and walls are regular repeating lines. They lack the per-tile scallops and highlights of the reference roofs, and the speckled plaster and individually shaded stones on the walls. The shutter door is a few flat grey bands with little grain. The outline is tinted, with no neutral dark edge pixels, so it is not a sticker look. Even so, the candidate is clearly thinner and more mechanical than the references in tonal depth and surface variation. It would look noticeably flatter next to them.

surfaces.part: gable front wall with vent, roll-up shutter and door

answer.evidence: The silhouette widens row by row from 3px at row 6 to 138px at row 26, forming two large sloped roof planes that meet at a central ridge. Their lower edges are drawn as bright, slanted edge lines at about rows 36-58, with a darker row below them. Under the roof is a vertical front wall of corrugated siding, about rows 45-110, with a vent, a roll-up shutter and a door. The roof is a real top surface and the wall is a front face of more than 3 rows.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a corrugated-metal warehouse with a ridged roof, a roll-up shutter door and a small side door. Its outline is a dark bluish-grey that leans toward the material, and the measured neutral share of dark edge pixels is 0%, so it is not a near-black sticker line. The roof shows about 5 grey steps with a gradient and ridge lines, the walls carry vertical corrugation, and the shutter has horizontal slats. Near-flat coverage is 0%. It reaches only 6 visible tones per tile against 12 and 10 for the references, and its raw total is 23 colours against 185 and 66. That is a clear gap. The surfaces are regular, with no per-tile highlights, speckle or grain breaking up the stripes, so they read more as clean gradients than hand-dotted texture. The wall and shutter are also close to uniform stripes. A careful artist would find it thinner than the references, though not flat or sticker-like.

surfaces.part: roof, left and right sloped planes with shingle rows meeting at a central ridge
front wall with gable triangle, roller shutter and wooden door

answer.evidence: The building has a large sloped roof, rows 6-59. Its two planes are tiled with shingle rows and widen from 3 px at row 6 to 138 px at row 26. A bright eave line runs along the bottom edge of the roof, at about rows 40-59, so this is evidence (c). Below it is a south wall of about 52 rows (rows 60-111). The wall carries a gable triangle with a vent, a roller shutter with horizontal slats, and a wooden door. This gives a top surface and a front face of 3+ rows. No isometric receding side face is drawn.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a corrugated-metal warehouse. Its roof has horizontal banding with a few grey steps, and the walls use vertical ribbing. The shutter has horizontal slats, and the door is plain wood. The measured facts show 6 visible tones per tile against 12 and 10 for the references, so it is about half as rich. There are no flat 5x5 fills, and the dark edges are tinted rather than neutral (0% near-neutral). The grey-blue outline is a dark tone of the adjacent material, which is acceptable. The main weakness is shading depth: roof, wall and shutter each use roughly 3-4 steps against the references' 5-6. They also lack per-tile highlights, speckle, and grain variation. The ribbing is regular and mechanical, with no wear, stains, or individually shaded elements. Next to the references it reads as thinner and flatter, so it fails on density and shading depth.

surfaces.part: roof left slope plane (shingle/corrugated rows, bright eave edge diagonal)
roof right slope plane (darker, shaded side, with ridge line at the centre)
front wall with gable, vent, roller shutter and wooden door

answer.evidence: The silhouette widens row by row from 3 px at row 6 to 138 px at row 26 and stays at 138 to row 59. That is a large sloped roof drawn as two planes, with a ridge line at x~52 and a lighter left plane and darker right plane. Both planes end in a bright eave edge line along the diagonal at rows ~40-58. Below it the vertical corrugated front wall runs from row 60 to 111, about 52 rows. It has a roller shutter, a small vent and a wooden door. The roof is a clear top surface (evidence c) and the front face is well over 3 rows, so it reads as three-quarter.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate has 6 visible tones per 16x16 tile against 12 and 10 for the references, and only 23 distinct colours in total against 185 and 66. That is about half the reference density. The roof and walls use few lightness steps, roughly 3-4 grey values. The roof has horizontal banding and the walls have vertical corrugation, so it is not flat-filled (0% near-flat). The outline is a dark grey-blue lean with some tint, not the neutral black the numbers would suggest (0% neutral), but it is a uniform dark band around the forms, closer to a sticker outline than the selective, material-toned edges in Beodeul. The references have per-tile highlights, plaster speckle and stone shading dot by dot. The candidate has none of this: its surfaces are regular stripes with no grain, speckle or per-element variation. The shutter door and the plain door are cleanly drawn but simple. Overall it is clean but visibly thinner and more mechanical than the references.
